title: Fancy Zones: Multiple windows of the same application snapping to the same zone
author: NsCW
summary: FancyZones restores multiple windows from the same browser or Electron application into one last-known zone instead of preserving distinct per-window placements.
next_action: Reproduce current multi-window restoration and capture which app/window identity fields FancyZones records for each window.

confidence.rationale: The behavior is widely confirmed, while the safe identity strategy remains uncertain.

judgment.rationale: Many users provide consistent multi-window examples and the documented setting is application-oriented, but current identity behavior and browser restore timing need verification.
evidence: Chrome, Edge, Obsidian, and CAD users report multiple same-process windows stacking in one zone after restart.
Disabling `Move newly created windows to their last known zone` avoids the stacking behavior but removes the desired automation.
Browser profile, kiosk, and app command-line variations do not reliably distinguish the windows for FancyZones.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce current multi-window restoration and capture which app/window identity fields FancyZones records for each window.

fix_assessment.rationale: The desired per-window identity contract is not established and may depend on application-provided properties unavailable during restore.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones restores multiple windows from the same browser or Electron application into one last-known zone instead of preserving distinct per-window placements.
known_information: The original environment uses seven monitors and multiple Edge and Chrome windows.
The symptom extends beyond browsers to Electron and CAD applications.
The setting currently describes the last zone location that an application was in.
inferences: AppZoneHistory may be applying an application-level identity before stable per-window information is available during session restore.
issue_context.analysis: Maintainer-side reproduction should establish whether the present code still collapses windows and what stable discriminator, if any, exists before a design is proposed.
initial_investigation: Read all thirteen live comments and the reported workarounds.
Separated browser restore limitations from the cross-application FancyZones stacking behavior.

actions.label: Reproduce same-app window stacking
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact performs no upstream write.

reproduce.title: Trace multiple same-application windows through session restore
prerequisites: Move newly created windows to their last known zone enabled
At least three windows from one application
setup: Place each same-application window in a different zone.
Configure the application to restore its prior windows after sign-in.
steps: Record the window titles, process IDs, application paths, and assigned zones before restart.
Restart Windows and restore the application session.
Record the order windows appear and the zone assigned to each.
Repeat with a second multi-window application to distinguish app-specific behavior.
reproduce.expected_result: Each restored window returns to its own prior zone, or the trace clearly identifies the identity collision that prevents it.
